rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes bi-l-haqq circumstantial to the reciter: recite while adhering to truth and sincerity.
rows.anchor: اتل ذلك حال كونك ملتبسا بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis makes it circumstantial to nabāʾ: the account is truthful and agrees with earlier scriptures, establishing proof of the Messenger’s mission.
rows.anchor: اتل نبأهما ملتبسا بالصدق موافقا لما في كتب الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis makes it an adjective of an implicit verbal noun: recite a recitation marked by truth and sincerity.
rows.anchor: اتل ذلك تلاوة ملتبسة بالحق والصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn suggests al-Zamakhsharī prefers the verbal-noun analysis, since he lists it first; in all three, bāʾ conveys accompaniment and attaches to an omitted phrase.
rows.anchor: وكأنه اختيار الزمخشري إذ به بدأ

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the mīm in Ādam with sukūn before bāʾ in al-ḥaqq; likewise any mīm preceded by a vowel and followed by bāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بسكون الميم من " آدم "

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
rows.claim: They attach idh to nabāʾ itself: the account is their story at that time; al-Samīn calls this clear.
rows.anchor: وبه بدأ الزمخشري وأبو البقاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats idh as a substitute for nabāʾ, supplying an omitted noun: “the account of that time.”
rows.anchor: نبأ ذلك الوقت، كذا قدره الزمخشري

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh rejects the substitution because idh can be annexed only to a time, whereas nabāʾ is not a time.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا يجوز ما ذكر

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ offers a third analysis: idh is circumstantial to nabāʾ and depends on an omitted phrase.
rows.anchor: أنه حال من " نبأ " وعلى هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn finds the third analysis unclear and agrees that idh cannot be a temporal adverb for the future command recite.
rows.anchor: لكن هذا الوجه غير واضح

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes qur bān as the name of something offered to draw near to God, analogizing it to ḥulwān, what is given.
rows.anchor: به قال الزمخشري - أنه اسم لما يتقرب به

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī cites “تقربوا قرف القمع” to show that taqarraba can take bāʾ and mean qarraba, supporting the proposed reflexive construction.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي: " تقربوا قرف القمع "

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: On this derivation, the wording implies “they offered it and so drew near by it”; al-Samīn judges this construction remote.
rows.anchor: إذ قرباه فتقربا به، وفيه بعد

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh objects that تقرب بصدقة is not the passive response to قرب صدقة: both verbs have the same agent, unlike true mutual or passive change.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وليس " تقرب بصدقة " مطاوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn challenges the Shaykh’s rule, saying he does not accept that account of the construction.
rows.anchor: لأنا لا نسلم هذه القاعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats qur bān as originally a verbal noun later applied to the thing offered, like “Yemeni weaving” and “the prince’s striking.”
rows.anchor: أن يكون في الأصل مصدرا ثم أطلق على الشيء المتقرب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its singular form supports the verbal-noun analysis: although Cain and Abel each had an offering, the original form would have been dual qur bānayn.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك أنه لم يثن والموضع موضع تثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker threatening murder is the brother whose offering was not accepted, addressing the brother whose offering was accepted.
rows.anchor: قال الذي لم يتقبل منه للمقبول منه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the threat with a doubled nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: " لأقتلنك " بالنون الشديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat is the answer to an omitted oath.
rows.anchor: وهذا جواب قسم محذوف، وقرأه زيد بالخفيفة

rows.speaker: زيد
rows.claim: Zayd reads the threat with a light nūn.
rows.anchor: قرأه زيد بالخفيفة. قال: إنما يتقبل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of “God accepts” is understood as their offerings and deeds.
rows.anchor: مفعوله محذوف لدلالة المعنى عليه أي: قرابينهم وأعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verb is used without an intended object, as in “as for one who gives and is mindful.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز ألا يراد له مفعول كقوله

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies an omitted exchange: why kill me when I have done no wrong and am not to blame for God accepting my offering instead of yours?
rows.anchor: قال أبو محمد بن عطية: " قبلها كلام محذوف

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another commentator also posits a lengthy ellipsis and gives a similar reconstruction.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: " فيه حذف يطول " وذكر نحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn sees no need for a long reconstruction: the threat arises from envy at the accepted offering, and the reply hints that piety is the cause of acceptance.
rows.anchor: إذ المعاني المفهومة من فحوى الكلام إذا قدرت قصيرة كان أحسن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the reply as telling the envious brother that he brought this on himself by shedding the garment of piety.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: كيف كان قوله: { إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn classifies al-Zamakhsharī’s explanation as interpretation of the meaning, not grammatical parsing.
rows.anchor: وهذا ونحوه من تفسير المعنى لا الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes the acceptance statement an interjection between the killer’s threat and the victim’s speech, with “he said” referring to God addressing the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن هذه الجملة اعتراض بين كلام القاتل وبين كلام المقتول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn calls the divine-interjection reading extremely remote because it disrupts the sequence of speech between Cain and Abel.
rows.anchor: وهو في غاية البعد لتنافر النظم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī answers that the singular means each one offered an offering, as in the command to flog each person eighty times.
rows.anchor: كما قاله أبو علي الفارسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in la-in is an oath-introducing lām; the reply answers an omitted oath, following the rule that the earlier of a condition and oath is answered.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله: { لئن }: هي الموطئة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that a verbal condition paired with an active participle in the response emphasizes refusal of this heinous act; bāʾ reinforces the negation.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: لم جاء الشرط بلفظ الفعل، والجزاء بلفظ اسم الفاعل وهو قوله: { لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني مآ أنا بباسط }؟ قلت: ليفيد

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh argues that “I am not one who stretches” answers the oath, not the condition; a negated conditional answer would need fa and violate the precedence rule.
rows.anchor: قال: " لأن هذا جواب للقسم لا للشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn rejects the criticism: al-Zamakhsharī calls it the condition’s consequence because it expresses that consequence, which is unobjectionable terminology.
rows.anchor: وهذا ليس بشيء لأن أبا القاسم سماه جزاء للشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn notes that al-Zamakhsharī elsewhere treated a similar response as answering the oath while standing in for the condition’s answer.
rows.anchor: وقد خالف الزمخشري كلامه هنا بما ذكره في البقرة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ṭawwaʿat with a doubled wāw and no alif.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على " طوعت " مشدد الواو من غير ألف

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: This reading means that the soul made the killing easy or prompted it.
rows.anchor: بمعنى " سهلت وبعثت "

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives the sense “made spacious and easy” from ṭāʿa lahu al-martaʿ, when pasture expands.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وسعته ويسرته من " طاع له المرتع " إذا اتسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn analyzes the doubled form as causative: killing initially yielded to the soul, and the doubled verb makes it an object, as with the hamza form.
rows.anchor: والتضعيف فيه للتعدية لأن الأصل: طاع له قتل أخيه

rows.speaker: الحسن وزيد بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and many others read ṭāwaʿat with an alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وزيد بن علي وجماعة كثيرة: " فطاوعت "

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows form III to mean form I without mutual action, citing paired examples; Sībawayh discusses this pattern.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري فيها احتمالين، أحدهما: أن يكون مما جاء فيه فاعل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Alternatively, he takes the form as reciprocal: killing called the soul to act, while the soul recoiled until killing overcame it and it yielded.
rows.anchor: جعل القتل يدعو إلى نفسه لأجل الحسد الذي لحق قابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase lahu attaches to ṭawwaʿat on either reading.
rows.anchor: " له " متعلق ب " طوعت " على القراءتين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls lahu an added connective: the clause would be complete without it, as in “I guarded Zayd’s property.”
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: و " له " لزيادة الربط

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects direct transitivity without the lām here, since that construction takes one object while the verse already has “the killing of his brother.”
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء " وقال قوم: طاوعت تتعدى بغير لام

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He also gives an alternative underlying construction: “his soul complied with him regarding the killing,” with the lām replacing omitted ʿalā.
rows.anchor: وقيل: التقدير: طاوعته نفسه على قتل أخيه، فزاد اللام وحذف " على "

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is nominal: Allāh is the predicate of “your guardian,” and “His Messenger” and “those who believe” are coordinated with the predicate.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر، و " رسوله " و " الذين " عطف على الخبر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the singular walī by presenting God’s guardianship as original and the Messenger’s and believers’ as following it.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: قد ذكرت جماعة فهلا قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn offers another explanation: the adjective faʿīl can have one form for masculine or feminine, singular, dual, or plural, as in “the men are a friend.”
rows.anchor: فعيل، وفعيل وقد نص عليه أهل اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that al-Zamakhsharī and others use the same explanation for “the people of Lot are not far from you.”
rows.anchor: وقد أجاب الزمخشري وغيره بذلك في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s wording “إنما مولاكم” is an explanatory gloss, not a reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: " إنما مولاكم " وهي تفسير لا قراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes “those who establish prayer” a nominative adjective of “those who believe,” describing believers through prayer and almsgiving, the two most excellent branches of faith.
rows.anchor: أنه مرفوع على الوصف لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis makes the phrase a nominative بدل of “those who believe.”
rows.anchor: الثاني: أنه مرفوع على البدل من " الذين آمنوا "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis supplies a new subject: “they are those who establish prayer.”
rows.anchor: الثالث: أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي: هم الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth analysis treats the phrase as an explanatory apposition; anything eligible as بدل can be بيان except previously specified cases.
rows.anchor: الرابع: أنه عطف بيان لما قبله؛ فإن كل ما جاز أن يكون بدلا جاز أن يكون بيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth analysis makes the phrase accusative under an omitted verb, cutting it off from the preceding dependent construction.
rows.anchor: الخامس: أنه منصوب بإضمار فعل، وهذا الوجه والذي قبله من باب القطع عن التبعية

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh asks why al-Zamakhsharī omitted the adjective analysis, which he considers immediate; he also argues that بدل presumes its antecedent could be dropped, impossible for a description on which later descriptions depend.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ:- بعد أن نقل عن الزمخشري وجهي البدل وإضمار المبتدأ فقط - " ولا أدري ما الذي منعه من الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn disputes the Shaykh: بدل is more immediate, a relative pronoun is not a derivative adjective in form, and he rejects the claim that بدل necessarily treats its antecedent as omitted, citing Sībawayh.
rows.anchor: قلت: لا نسلم أن المتبادر إلى الذهن الوصف بل البدل هو المتبادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearer analysis coordinates this nominal sentence with the preceding clauses, making it part of the relative clause.
rows.anchor: في هذه الجملة وجهان، أظهرهما: أنها معطوفة على ما قبلها من الجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses a nominal sentence rather than “and they bow” to highlight bowing as the most evident pillar of prayer.
rows.anchor: وجاء بهذه الجملة اسمية دون ما قبلها، فلم يقل " ويركعون " اهتماما بهذا الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wāw is circumstantial, with the subject being the wāw in “they give”; rukūʿ means humility toward the poor recipients.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنها واو الحال وصاحبها هو واو " يؤتون " والمراد بالركوع الخضوع

rows.speaker: علي أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: Rukūʿ may be literal: a report says that ʿAlī, Commander of the Faithful, gave his ring in charity while bowing.
rows.anchor: كما روي عن علي أمير المؤمنين أنه تصدق بخاتمه وهو راكع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is a conditional noun in the nominative as the sentence’s subject.
rows.anchor: من شرط في محل رفع بالابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes “God’s party are the triumphant” the conditional answer, supporting grammarians who do not require a resumptive pronoun for a conditional subject.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون جوابا للشرط، وبه يحتج من لا يشترط عود ضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection is that God’s party repeats the meaning of the conditional subject; al-Akhfash permits such repetition, with an understood pronoun and divine affiliation honoring the party.
rows.anchor: إنما جاز ذلك لأن المراد بحزب الله هو نفس المبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the answer is omitted and understood as becoming part of God’s triumphant party or being helped; the following clause indicates it.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الجواب محذوفا لدلالة الكلام عليه أي: ومن يتول الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is in the jussive position if it is the conditional answer; it has no syntactic position if it merely indicates an omitted answer.
rows.anchor: في محل جزم إن جعلناه جوابا للشرط، ولا محل له إن جعلناه دالا على الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They” can be a pronoun of separation, or a new subject whose predicate is “the triumphant”; that sentence then predicates the إن clause.
rows.anchor: وقوله: " هم " يحتمل أن يكون فصلا وأن يكون مبتدأ و " الغالبون " خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥizb means a distinct group marked by force and severity.
rows.anchor: والحزب: الجماعة فيها غلظة وشدة، فهو جماعة خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Furādā is accusative as a circumstantial phrase describing the subject of “you came to Us.”
rows.anchor: منصوب على الحال من فاعل " جئتمونا "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past verb may express a future event assured to happen, as with “God’s command has come” and “the people of Paradise called.”
rows.anchor: أنه بمعنى المستقبل أي: تجيئوننا، وإنما أبرزه في صورة الماضي لتحققه كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verb is past and depicts the scene from the perspective of the day they are told this, when their coming is already past.
rows.anchor: أنه ماض والمراد به حكاية الحال بين يدي الله تعالى يوم يقال لهم ذلك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows furādā to be a plural of several forms: fard, farīd, fard, and fardān.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء: " فرادى جمع فرد وفريد وفرد وفردان "

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives it as the plural of fardān, on the pattern of sukkārā from sukkārān and ʿujālā from ʿajlān.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: " هو جمع فردان ك سكران وسكارى، وعجلان وعجالى "

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib reports the derivation as plural of farīd, like radīf/radāfā and asīr/asārā.
rows.anchor: هو جمع فريد كرديف وردافى، وأسير وأسارى، قاله الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others derive it from fard with either a fatḥa or sukūn on the rāʾ; on this account its alif is feminine like those in sukkārā and asārā, so it is diptote.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو جمع فرد بفتح الراء، وقيل بسكونها، وعلى هذا فألفه للتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some classify it as a collective noun because fard does not regularly form this plural; those calling it a plural mean that semantically, “one by one.”
rows.anchor: لأن فردا لا يجمع على فرادى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression means “one by one”; an anonymous poetic line uses furādā alongside “in pairs” as evidence for this sense.
rows.anchor: ومعنى فرادى: فردا فردا، فإذا قلت: جاء القوم فرادى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Related usage includes farada yaf rudu furūdan, fārid, afrad, and feminine fardāʾ; its plural is fard, like ḥumr from aḥmar/aḥmarāʾ.
rows.anchor: ويقال: فرد يفرد فرودا فهو فارد وأفردته أنا، ورجل أفرد

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر وأبو حيوة
rows.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Abū Ḥaywa read furādan, the declinable form used in Tamīm.
rows.anchor: وهي لغة تميم، وبها قرأ عيسى بن عمر وأبو حيوة

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ records a rare anomalous reading with tanwīn, treating فراد as a sound noun, a rare plural like nuwwām and rijāl.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء " وقرئ في الشاذ بالتنوين على أنه اسم صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another anomalous reading is فراد without tanwīn, indeclinable like aḥād and rubāʿ as a shifted adjective.
rows.anchor: ويقال أيضا: " جاء القوم فراد " غير منصرف فهو كأحاد

rows.speaker: خارجة عن نافع وأبي عمرو
rows.claim: Khārija reports that Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr read fardā, analogizing the group to a feminine collective as in “you see people drunk.”
rows.anchor: وروى خارجة عن نافع وأبي عمرو كليهما أنهما قرآ " فردى " مثل سكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf may be circumstantial to the subject of “you came to Us”; grammarians who reject multiple circumstances instead treat it as a substitute for furādā.
rows.anchor: أنها منصوبة المحل على الحال من فاعل " جئتمونا "

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: A second analysis makes the kāf an adjective of an omitted verbal noun; Makkī estimates “coming singly, a singleness like your state when first created.”
rows.anchor: وقدره مكي: " منفردين انفرادا/ مثل حالكم أول مرة "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn prefers the direct circumstantial analysis because the verb indicates its verbal noun more strongly than a descriptive word does.
rows.anchor: والأول أحسن لأن دلالة الفعل على المصدر أقوى

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ makes the kāf circumstantial to the implicit subject of furādā, estimating “resembling your initial creation.”
rows.anchor: كذا قدره أبو البقاء، وفيه نظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn objects that they do not resemble their initial creation; the estimate should supply “your state” as the comparison.
rows.anchor: وصوابه أن تقدر مضافا أي: مشبهة حالكم حال ابتداء خلقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awwala marratin is a time adverb governed by khalaqnākum; marra was originally the verbal noun of marra yamurru, then broadened to mean a time.
rows.anchor: منصوب على ظرف الزمان والعامل فيه

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says the usage shows how closely a time expression resembles a verb.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " وهذا يدل

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh rejects treating marra as “the first creation,” since that implies a second creation; the event is a return or recreation.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " وانتصب " أول مرة " على الظرف أي: أول زمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-taraktum may be an accusative circumstantial clause with an implicit qad, or an independent clause with no syntactic position.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنها في محل نصب على الحال من فاعل " جئتمونا "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is the object of taraka; min is a relative pronoun, while treating it as an indefinite noun with an omitted resumptive is weaker.
rows.anchor: ويضعف جعلها نكرة موصوفة والعائد محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taraka takes one object here because it means “leave”; if given the sense “make,” it would take two objects.
rows.anchor: ولو ضمنت معنى صير تعدت لاثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwala takes two objects because it means to give and grant possession.
rows.anchor: يتعدى لاثنين لأنه بمعنى أعطى وملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khawl means the blessings God granted; khawwalkahu means “I gave him ownership of the khawl,” like mawaltuhu al-māl.
rows.anchor: والخول: ما أعطاه الله من النعم

rows.speaker: أبو النجم
rows.claim: Abū al-Najm’s verse uses khawl in the phrase khawli al-mukhawwal as lexical evidence.
rows.anchor: قال أبو النجم: 1988 كوم الذرى من خول

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says takhwīl originally means giving khawl; alternatively it is giving what becomes one’s responsibility or what needs caretaking.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب: " والتخويل في الأصل: إعطاء الخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warāʾa ẓuhūrikum attaches to taraktum; alternatively, taraka means “made,” taking the relative object and this locative as its two objects.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يضمن " ترك " هنا معنى صير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second parsing, the meaning is that they made what God granted them into something left behind their backs.
rows.anchor: أي: وصيرتم الترك الذي خولناكموه كائنا وراء ظهوركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading of narā is visual perception taking one object, with maʿakum attached to it.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنها المتعدية لواحد فهي بصرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Narā could instead mean “know,” taking two objects; the second would be a locative meaning “present with you.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى علم، فيتعدى لاثنين

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ considers the “know” analysis weak because “we do not know your intercessors with you” is not intended.
rows.anchor: إلا أن أبا البقاء استضعف هذا الوجه وهو كما قال

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects taking maʿakum as circumstantial to the intercessors, which he thinks would mean they are present but unseen.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " ولا يجوز أن يكون أي معكم حالا من الشفعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn replies that negating a qualified entity can deny either the entity itself or only its qualification; the wording need not mean the intercessors are present but unseen.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن النفي إذا دخل على ذات بقيد ففيه وجهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn points to his earlier treatment of this construction in the opening of al-Baqara and at “they do not ask people persistently.”
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم تحقيق هذه القاعدة في أوائل البقرة وفي قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause anna-hum fills both object slots of zaʿamtum, and fīkum attaches to shurakāʾ.
rows.anchor: و " أنهم " ساد مسد المفعولين ل " زعم "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged intercessors are said to be partners with God concerning the people’s worship or creation, since the people associated them with God in both.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: الذين زعمتم أنهم شركاء لله فيكم أي: في عبادتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed reading takes fī as “with” or “in the presence of,” but al-Samīn says it is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وقيل " في " بمعنى " عند " ولا حاجة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation makes them partners in the people’s punishment, sharing it if the people believed they would share their calamities.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أنهم يتحملون عنكم نصيبا من العذاب

rows.speaker: نافع والكسائي وعاصم في رواية حفص
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and ʿĀṣim in Ḥafṣ’s transmission read baynakum in the accusative; the rest read it in the nominative.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع والكسائي وعاصم في رواية حفص عنه: " بينكم " نصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the accusative reading, the strongest analysis supplies an implicit subject meaning “connection,” inferred from the mention of partners; baynakum is adverbial.
rows.anchor: والاتصال وإن لم يكن مذكورا

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash makes baynakum the subject while retaining its usual accusative form as an adverb; similar examples include 60:3 and 72:11.
rows.anchor: على أغلب أحواله وهو مذهب الأخفش

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains that an adverb frequently used in the accusative may retain that form when syntactically nominative.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي: " كما جرى في كلامهم منصوبا ظرفا، تركوه

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh describes the word as built on its common adverbial form, but al-Samīn objects that frequency is not a recognized cause of indeclinability; the Shaykh also suggests annexation to an indeclinable word.
rows.anchor: وفي كلام الشيخ لما حكى مذهب الأخفش ما يصرح بأنه مبني فإنه قال: " وخرجه الأخفش على أنه فاعل ولكنه مبني

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ supplies an omitted subject described by baynakum, estimating “a connection between you has been severed.”
rows.anchor: أن الفاعل محذوف، و " بينكم " صفة له قامت مقامه

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh objects that a subject cannot be omitted; al-Samīn replies that Abū al-Baqāʾ means it is unexpressed while its substitute stands in its place.
rows.anchor: ورده الشيخ بأن الفاعل لا يحذف

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya likewise supplies an omitted subject such as “connection” or “bond”; al-Samīn calls the analysis clear.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " ويكون الفعل مسندا إلى شيء محذوف

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s omitted-subject account on the grounds stated above.
rows.anchor: ورده الشيخ بما تقدم. ويجاب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth analysis makes baynakum the subject, indeclinable because it is annexed to a nondeclinable word.
rows.anchor: الرابع: أن " بينكم " هو الفاعل، وإنما بني لإضافته إلى غير متمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic example keeps mithla fatḥa although it is attached to the nominative damm, illustrating this analysis.
rows.anchor: مثل ما أثمر حماض الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second anonymous line has ghayra in the accusative form even though it is the subject of yamnaʿ.
rows.anchor: حمامة في غصون ذات أوقال بفتح " غير " وهي فاعل

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s line has maqālata with fatḥa though it substitutes for a nominative clause, because it is annexed to indeclinable أن and its clause.
rows.anchor: قول النابغة: 1991 أتاني أبيت اللعن أنك لمتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both taqaṭṭaʿa and ḍalla seek “what you used to claim” as subject. Basrans prefer applying the later verb; Kufans prefer the earlier one.
rows.anchor: و " ضل " كلاهما يتوجهان على

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: On the Basran preference to apply the later verb, ḍalla raises mā; taqaṭṭaʿa receives an implicit subject and governs baynakum as an adverb.
rows.anchor: فعلى اختيار البصريين يكون " ضل " هو الرفع ل " ما كنتم تزعمون "

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: On the Kufan preference to apply the earlier verb, taqaṭṭaʿa raises mā and ḍalla has an implicit subject; baynakum remains an adverb governed by taqaṭṭaʿa.
rows.anchor: وعلى اختيار الكوفيين يكون " تقطع " هو الرافع ل " ما كنتم تزعمون "

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: A further analysis supplies a deleted relative noun, “what is between you”; Kufan grammarians allow this omission and cite Arabic poetry.
rows.anchor: أن الظرف صلة لموصول محذوف تقديره: تقطع ما بينكم

rows.speaker: عبد الله ومجاهد والأعمش
rows.claim: The reading “لقد تقطع ما بينكم” reported from ʿAbd Allāh, Mujāhid, and al-Aʿmash supports supplying the deleted relative noun.
rows.anchor: قراءة عبد الله ومجاهد والأعمش: { لقد تقطع ما بينكم }

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī paraphrases the clause as “the severing occurred between you,” construing the verb as predicated of its verbal noun by interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " لقد تقطع بينكم: لقد وقع التقطع بينكم

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh objects that this requires deleting the subject or using a verb and subject with the same sense, lacking distinct predicate and subject.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الشيخ اعترض فقال: " وظاهره أنه ليس بجيد

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh adds that “the severing severed” would also imply the opposite of the intended meaning, as if connection had resulted.
rows.anchor: أنه يلزم عليه أيضا فساد المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn says the Shaykh’s objection does not refute al-Zamakhsharī because the latter explicitly bases the parse on the stated interpretive paraphrase.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي أورده الشيخ وقررته من كلامه حتى فهم لا يرد
